correctness.rationale: The (21,5,1) difference set has all twenty ordered nonzero differences and defines the stated plane. Translation is free on vertices and edges, with exactly one orbit of noncollinear triangles with order-three stabilizer. On its closed triangle the stabilizer acts by rotation; the quotient is a disk, and the quotient of the boundary traverses the step-seven edge only once. Giving every other triangle orbit its ordinary characteristic disk yields the actual CW orbit space with (1,10,54) cells. Reconstructing all 54 step-words and implementing the specified greedy reductions independently gives the nine stated substitutions. Each selected pivot word after earlier substitutions uses its pivot edge exactly once, giving a homotopy equivalence relative to the other graph edges in the graph plus pivot disk; the other attachments are transported by that equivalence. There remain 31 empty words, nine seventh powers and five inverse seventh powers on e₁. After the first degree-seven disk, 44 residual maps are null. This proves the homotopy decomposition for the nonfree ordinary quotient.
residual_risks: The original C₂₁ action is not a universal covering action. The computation is finite for the specified design and not a formal proof-assistant result.

value.rationale: This is the natural first nonfree example, and the orbit-disk correction is a good illustration of why a free computation would fail. Neither the exceptional-stabilizer phenomenon nor the resulting invariants are new here; the asserted classification is a routine consequence of the classical two-complex theorem. No new marked or equivariant structure beyond that classification is supplied.
residual_risks: A future, separate claim about an equivariant or marked object would need its own proof and value assessment.
